newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-BARECLONA'S ROBSON FACES TACTICAL DILEMMA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BARECLONA'S ROBSON FACES TACTICAL DILEMMA.

text.p: By Richard Bastin
Barcelona's league game at Logrones this Sunday is being seen as an acid test of whether coach Bobby Robson has what it takes to give leaders Real Madrid a run for their money.

The extraordinary 5-4 midweek Spanish Cup victory over Atletico Madrid at the Camp Nou -- in which Robson's men came back from 3-0 and 4-2 down -- has given disgruntled Barcelona fans a glimmer of hope.
They had been shouting insults at Robson, goalkeeper Vitor Baia and club chairman Jose Luis Nunez but ended the game euphoric after one of the most remarkable comebacks ever seen in Spain.
The match drew praise even from controversial Atletico owner Jesus Gil, who had threatened to withdraw his team from the competition in a row over player suspensions.
"It was one of the best sporting spectacles in recent years," said Gil.
After going 3-0 down after 30 minutes, Robson brought on extra strikers, and saw the gamble pay dividends as Juan Pizzi, Luis Figo and Ronaldo -- who scored a fine hat-trick -- turned the tables.
"It's a night for the players as they've behaved like heroes," said the former England coach.
But the question marks remain as to whether Robson is prepared to take the same risks to close the nine-point gap on Real in the remaining 14 league games.
"I need time to think about what has happened tonight as we played very risky football," he said.
The dilemma has been heightened by the fact that Barcelona's second place, and with it a slot in next season's European Cup, has come under threat.
Barcelona lead unfancied Real Betis only on goal difference, while a rejuvenated Deportivo Coruna are snapping at their heels three points back.
So Robson may choose to play safe and hang on to second, or go out with all guns blazing in a bid to take the title.
Although fiery Bulgarian striker Hristo Stoichkov has now staked his claim to a regular place, Robson is still faced by the age-old question over whether to use Ivan de la Pena.
The 20-year old has combined superbly in the last two games with another shaven-headed darling of the Camp Nou, Brazilian prodigy Ronaldo.
But de la Pena mixes his defence-splitting through balls with an unreliability that borders on carelessness.
And Robson knows that any more upsets like the 4-0 defeat at Tenerife two weeks ago could cost him his job.
But if he does follow the attacking route, Robson knows that there could hardly be a better place than Logrones to begin the experiment.
Barcelona thrashed the Rioja side 8-0 in the Camp Nou earlier in the season.
And Barca make the return trip this Sunday knowing that a victory would be a great way to put some pressure on leaders Real Madrid, who play a tough game at sixth-placed Real Sociedad on Monday.
Real Betis visit Rayo Vallecano on Sunday -- three days after playing the same side in the Spanish Cup on the same muddy Madrid pitch.
Betis have the best away record in the league and will need another victory to keep up the pressure.
Deportivo have yet to lose under new coach Carlos Alberto Silva and visit struggling Espanyol, who were knocked out of the cup by second division Las Palmas on Wednesday.
